length.text: About 51 to 117 cm; record about 147 cm

diet.text: Lizards, snakes, reptile eggs and small rodents

overview.text: The Western Patch-nosed Snake is a harmless snake of the deserts of the south-western United States and northern Mexico, with a big curved scale over its nose.

identification.text: A thick scale curves back over the top of the snout like a patch. Yellowish with blackish stripes along the sides.

size.label: Adults
size.text: Usually 51 to 117 cm (20 to 46 in); the record is 58 in.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: Arizona, southern California, Nevada, Utah, southern New Mexico and south-western Texas, and northern Mexico including Baja California.

diet.text: Lizards, snakes, reptile eggs and small rodents.

reproduction.text: Lays 4 to 10 eggs in spring or early summer; they hatch in August or September.

recognise.text: Patch-like curved scale on the tip of the nose.
